chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu 'Amirah, from Abd al-Rahman al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) did not see any harm in al-'azl (coitus interruptus).

And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify against themselves, [saying to them], 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we have testified.'
So everything from which the covenant was taken is released (from the obligation of consent), even if it were on a solid rock.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for the permissibility of coitus interruptus (azl) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn’s permissibility of 'azl by linking it to the Covenant of Alast (7:172), arguing that since God extracted the primordial testimony of lordship from all descendants of Adam, the potential for offspring is inherently acknowledged even before birth. This theological grounding implies that the right to choose non-procreation is rooted in the universal human condition established at the moment of creation, extending even to those incapable of explicit verbal consent.
